title: tjvz item
description: A reading item: one record in the feed cache, the stack, an archive month-shard, or a trash month-shard. Every source adapter produces this shape via canonicalise(). Archive records are self-sufficient for re-broadcast as a reader RSS feed (see schema/README.md 'Archive records as a broadcast RSS feed'). See README.md for field prose, the format vocabulary, and the inbox drop format. tjvz's built-in validator enforces the subset {type, required, enum, properties, items, oneOf, additionalProperties}; the rest (pattern, format, const, minItems, ...) is for external JSON Schema tooling.

schema_version.description: Record schema version. Always 1 today. store.py applies MIGRATIONS on read when this lags the current version.

id.description: tjvz-assigned, never taken from the source. 'u:' + sha256(canonical_url)[:16] when a URL exists, else 't:' + sha256(normalised title + first author)[:16]. id_scheme is a frozen constant (1); a bump invalidates cross-user id joins loudly.

url.description: The item URL exactly as the source gave it. null only for URL-less items (some AI-authored inbox records).

canonical_url.description: url after tracking-param stripping and host rewriting. The dedup key and the basis of a 'u:' id. null iff url is null.

authors.description: Every creator, in source order. A bare string is accepted on input and normalised to {name, role: 'author'}. role defaults to 'author'; Zotero contributes 'editor'/'translator'/'contributor'/'commenter'/... Features that care filter to role == 'author' themselves.

publication.description: Where it was published. RSS: channel <title>. Zotero: the publicationTitle base field (blogTitle / websiteTitle / bookTitle all map to it). Falls back to the canonical host, then the literal string 'unknown'. A model input, so it must always resolve to something.

format.description: tjvz's own vocabulary. RSS items default to 'essay' ('podcast'/'video' if an audio/video enclosure is present). Zotero itemTypes map per the table in README.md. 'other' is the last resort. The first eight are 'scorable' (they enter the TF-IDF / relevance corpus); the rest are not.

tags.description: Lowercased at storage. RSS <category> elements + Zotero tags; Zotero collection names are merged in too unless config zotero.collections_as_tags is false. Hyphen expansion (urdu-hindi -> urdu, hindi) happens at feature-computation time, not here.

summary.description: Short blurb. RSS <description> (the deck/subtitle only) or Zotero abstractNote. Not the body.

published.description: When the world got it. ISO-8601 preferred; partial values tolerated ('2024', '2024-08'). RSS <pubDate> (RFC 822, converted). Zotero 'date' is free text and is best-effort parsed. Never backfilled.

text_ref.description: sha256 (hex) of the extracted plain-text body. The bytes live at .tjvz/text/<first two hex chars>/<hash>.txt, which is a per-profile cache (safe to lose). Body text is never stored inline in the record.

text_source.description: Which text tier is available for this item, best to worst. Recorded from v0 on (even though v0 relevance is tags-only) so it is present when TF-IDF arrives.

source.description: Provenance. 'kind' is always present. kind=rss adds feed_id, feed_url, guid. kind=zotero adds library, key, version. kind=jsonfile adds path. kind=csv adds path (and optionally row). kind=manual needs only kind. Extra provenance keys are allowed.

aliases.description: Other canonical_urls known to be the same item (m./AMP/custom-domain variants). Filled by `tjvz dedup`, not by adapters.

first_seen.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the first time tjvz ingested this item, in this profile.

read.description: When you read it. Set only on archive records; null everywhere else. ISO-8601, partial tolerated ('2026-05'). Set by `tjvz read` (a full UTC timestamp) or an importer (Zotero dateAdded / Reading-Flow date, a CSV's date column). Mutually exclusive with `dismissed`. Becomes the broadcast feed's <pubDate>.

dismissed.description: When you dismissed it. Set only on trash records; null everywhere else. ISO-8601 UTC timestamp. Mutually exclusive with `read`. Kept so a dismissal can be reviewed or undone without the record living in the archive.

blurb.description: Your own one-line take on the item, written for the broadcast RSS feed (becomes/leads the <description>). Distinct from `summary`, which is the source's own blurb. Optional; null unless you wrote one.

rating.description: YOUR rating, an integer 1-5. Set by `tjvz rate <id> <1-5>`. null / absent = unrated. Never backfilled. Feeds the avg_rating features (an unrated read is imputed as 3); broadcast verbatim.

readers.description: OTHER people's signals about this item - from a friend's broadcast feed, or an AI drop in inbox/. Keyed by `source`; re-ingesting the same source updates its entry. The substrate for the reader_avg_rating feature (feature 4). Kept strictly separate from your own `rating`. Empty on most records.

source.description: Whose signal this is: a broadcast feed id, a person's handle, 'ai:<name>', ...

rating.description: Their rating, 1-5 (an adapter converts other scales at ingest). null = they surfaced it without rating (a curator).

ext.description: Open extension bag. New sources and future features add keys here without a schema migration. Common keys are typed below; anything else is allowed.

collection_tags.description: The normalised subset of `tags` that came from Zotero collection names (present only when zotero.collections_as_tags is on). broadcast.share_tags: no-collections drops exactly these from the emitted <category> list.
